# Bukas Cafe

> Bukas Cafe is a Filipino progressive cafe at 56-14 Van Horn St, Elmhurst, Queens, NY 11373. Owned by Elmhurst locals Anna Javier and Angel Carreon, it serves progressive Filipino drinks and comfort food — signature lattes like the Bukas Na (salted cream, asin tibuok) and Ube Eclipse, an espresso series called Clouds Over MNL, Japan-grown matcha milled in the Philippines, and kitchen items like the Adobo Jalapeño Melt. "Bukas" means both "tomorrow" and "open" in Tagalog. Open Wednesday–Sunday from 9:00 AM (until 3:00 PM Wednesday and Thursday, 6:00 PM Friday through Sunday), closed Monday and Tuesday. Dine-in and takeout, no delivery, typically $10–20 per person. Phone: (929) 781-4080. Email: hello@bukascafe.com. Instagram: @bukas.cafe. Ranked the #1 new NYC coffee & tea spot of 2026 on Beli.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.bukascafe.com/): Story, signature menu highlights, reviews, press, location and hours
- [Menu](https://www.bukascafe.com/menu.html): Full menu — espresso, signature lattes, tea, matcha, non-coffee drinks, food, and add-ons with prices
- [Events](https://www.bukascafe.com/events.html): Pop-ups and community events, including collabs and after-hours nights
- [Sa’yo ang Bukas](https://www.bukascafe.com/sayo-ang-bukas.html): The story behind the café’s free pop-up program — a dedicated day when Bukas opens free of charge to creatives, small businesses, bakers, makers and artists
- [A Few Things to Know](https://www.bukascafe.com/sayo-ang-bukas-guidelines.html): Sa’yo ang Bukas pop-up guidelines — a $100 operations and cleaning fee, limited weekday dates, a 16-person capacity, off-site food prep only, participant-run cleaning and promotion, and how to send a proposal to hello@bukascafe.com
